routes.label: Express two angles using one base angle

question:
In the figure \(AB=AC,\) angle \(BAD=30^\circ,\) and \(AE=AD.\) Then angle \(CDE\) equals:

[Figure 1](figures/1956_AMC_12_Q24_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The two isosceles triangles let us express both angles at \(D\) using the same base angle. Their difference will give \(\angle CDE\).

Let \(b=\angle ABC=\angle BCA\), where the equality follows from \(AB=AC\). The triangle angle sum gives
\[
\angle BAC=180^\circ-2b.
\]
The figure places \(D\) between \(B\) and \(C\), and \(E\) on side \(AC\). Since \(\angle BAD=30^\circ\),
\[
\angle DAE=\angle DAC=150^\circ-2b.
\]
Now \(AD=AE\), so triangle \(ADE\) has equal base angles. Consequently,
\[
\angle ADE=\frac{180^\circ-(150^\circ-2b)}2
=15^\circ+b.
\]
In triangle \(ACD\), the angles at \(A\) and \(C\) are \(150^\circ-2b\) and \(b\). Hence
\[
\angle ADC=180^\circ-(150^\circ-2b)-b
=30^\circ+b.
\]
Ray \(DE\) lies inside \(\angle ADC\), so subtracting removes the unknown base angle:
\[
\angle CDE=\angle ADC-\angle ADE
=(30^\circ+b)-(15^\circ+b)=15^\circ.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{15^\circ}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
